stories.deck: A major KFC franchisee, has filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection citing financial difficulties. The company seeks to restructure its operations and avoid losing its franchise agreement with Yum Brands. Tasty Chick’n has closed 44 restaurant locations this year and may shut down more in the future. The franchisee owes approximately $16 million in unpaid royalties to its parent company, Yum…
stories.bodyText:
A major KFC franchisee in the US has filed for bankruptcy protection, citing rising costs and declining sales, after shutting dozens of restaurants this year. The company has warned that more outlets could close as it seeks to restructure its operations and exit additional leases.
However, it alleged that the franchisee’s sudden restaurant closures had significantly damaged the KFC brand, leaving it absent from some markets and weakening its presence and consumer confidence in those communities.
In September, a major Wendy’s franchisee sought court protection while owing more than $147 million in royalties and fees to the burger chain’s corporate owner.
Pranjal Pandey is a journalist with the editorial desk of The Times of India (Online). He looks at the implications of global events for India, with a particular interest in geopolitics and defence. You can sometimes find him looking at the world map, wondering what’s new.

stories.headline: Rupee slides 8 paise to 93.49 against US dollar in early trade
stories.bodyText: Mumbai: The rupee slipped 8 paise to 93.49 against the US dollar in early trade on Thursday, weighed down by a strong greenback and weak domestic equity markets. . However, lower crude oil prices and foreign-fund inflows capped the rupee's fall, forex traders said. . At the interbank foreign exchange market, the rupee opened at 93.40 and declined to 93.49 against the greenback, registering a loss of 8 paise from its previous close. . The domestic currency climbed 10 paise to close at 93.41 against US dollar on Wednesday after gaining 68 paise in the preceding two sessions. .Rupee rises 7 paise to close at 93.44 against US dollar. "The decline in crude prices and RBI's actions to curb speculative activity in the currency have helped the rupee gain strength. In the near-term, the rupee is likely to trade in the 93.20 to 94 range," said V K Vijayakumar, Chief Investment Strategist, Geojit Investments. . According to Kaveri More, Commodity Technical Analyst at Choice Broking, the rupee was supported by foreign equity inflows and softer crude oil prices. However, further appreciation may remain limited due to India's high dependence on oil imports, a widening trade deficit, rising inflationary pressures, a stronger US dollar and elevated US Treasury yields. . "From a technical perspective, USD/INR could move towards the 92.20–91.70 range if the rupee sustains its current strength. On the upside, any corrective recovery in the dollar could push USD/INR towards 94.20–95.30," More said. . Meanwhile, the dollar index, which gauges the greenback's strength against a basket of six currencies, was at 103.90, higher by 0.11 per cent. . Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, was trading 0.26 per cent lower at $91.71 per barrel in futures trade. . On the domestic equity market front, Sensex declined 166.65 points or 0.20 per cent to 81,865.16 in early trade while Nifty fell 71.70 points or 0.26 per cent to 25,156.25. . Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) bought equities worth Rs 5,866.78 crore on Wednesday, according to exchange data.

stories.headline: ‘Revolution, not election’: SP's Azam Khan, on interim bail, predicts 'deluge' in upcoming UP polls
stories.deck: Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan, after receiving interim bail, declared the upcoming Uttar Pradesh Assembly polls a revolution. He criticized constitutional bodies for diminishing public faith and referenced historical educationists to highlight injustice. Khan emphasized that voters will focus on real issues rather than religion and caste in the elections. He expressed readiness to fight for…
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: 
Samajwadi Party
 leader 
Azam Khan
 has called the upcoming Uttar Pradesh Assembly polls a “revolution, not an election” after walking out of jail on interim bail in a money laundering case linked to his Mohammad Ali Jauhar University.
“This time there will be no election, there will be a revolution. There will be no change, there will be a deluge,” Khan told reporters on reaching his hometown Rampur late Wednesday night, PTI reported.
The Allahabad High Court granted Khan interim bail on Tuesday. The 
Enforcement Directorate
 (ED) had detained him on October 31, following which a PMLA court in Ghaziabad sent him to 14 days of judicial custody.
Reacting to his release, the senior SP leader said the court’s decision reinforced his belief that while the country was free, the Constitution remained in captivity. “With all of us together, we should demand the freedom of the Constitution,” he said.
On the upcoming elections, Khan said voters would no longer rally around religion and caste but around real issues. “We were ready to die for the Constitution and the law; we are ready and will remain ready,” he said.

When asked about Akhilesh Yadav’s promise that he would get justice once the SP formed a government, Khan replied: “Justice is justice, but no one would be subjected to revenge.”
Taking a jibe at the ED, Khan said that if someone accused of stealing chickens, goats and buffaloes could stand up to the agency and still build a university, he hoped every street would have a “chicken thief” who could do the same.
He also said constitutional bodies must look inward at why public faith in them is falling, and at the remarks the high courts and the Supreme Court have made about them. In a sarcastic aside, he claimed that if the ED, CBI, Income Tax Department and development authorities had existed in the days of educationists Madan Mohan Malaviya and Sir Syed Ahmad Khan, both would have been sent to jail too.

stories.headline: As three-year mark nears, Bhajan Lal Sharma seeks to shed ‘Parchi CM’ tag
stories.deck: Having entered office with virtually no administrative experience, his tenure has been a continuous tightrope walk between balancing the demands of the party’s central leadership and build authority of his own within the State.
stories.bodyText:
When Bhajan Lal Sharma, a first-time MLA who had largely remained in the background of the BJP’s Rajasthan unit, was named Chief Minister in December 2023, Congress State president Govind Singh Dotasara dismissed him as the “Parchi CM”, a leader chosen by the party’s central leadership rather than one who had built a political base of his own.
Nearly three years later, Mr. Dotasara has changed his line of attack. He now accuses the Mr. Sharma of being a leader “jisne poori BJP ko Rajasthan me khatam kar dala” (who has finished off the entire BJP in Rajasthan).

Keralam’s 15th Five-Year-Plan: Govt to explore possibilities in small modular reactors in the ‘longer-term’
briefs.deck: Keralam will assess SMRs for ‘feasibility, safety, siting and grid implications,’ according to the Approach Paper drafted by the State Planning Board
briefs.bodyText:
Keralam will explore, among other options, the possibilities offered by nuclear energy for energy security in the longer-term, according to the Approach Paper to the 15th Five Year Plan (for the 2027-2032 period) published on Wednesday.
“For the longer term, the State will assess small modular reactors (SMR) for feasibility, safety, siting and grid implications,” the Approach Paper drafted by the State Planning Board said. Elsewhere, the paper observed that systematic investment in local battery energy storage systems (BESS), large BESS, pumped storage and modular reactors is the way forward given that Keralam generates only 25% of its electricity demand internally.
The Approach Paper said Keralam will aim for an “informed decision” on the subject, “with the option kept open.” “This is a Union subject, and the State’s role covers siting, grid readiness and engagement,” it said. Green hydrogen and offshore wind will be assessed on the same basis. Alongside energy storage, the Plan also will promote household and decentralised generation.
SMRs are an evolving technology. According to the International Atomic Energy Agency’s (IAEA) definition, they are nuclear reactors with a power capacity of up to 300 MWe, about one-third the capacity of conventional nuclear reactors. In India, under the Nuclear Energy Mission announced in the 2025-26 Union Budget, ₹20,000 crore has been earmarked for research, design, development and deployment of SMRs. According to the Union government, the Department of Atomic Energy is working on the 220 MWe Bharat Small Modular Reactor (BSMR-200), the 55 MWe Small Modular Reactor (SMR-55) and a high-temperature gas-cooled reactor for hydrogen generation.
Proposals for establishing a nuclear power plant in Keralam in the 1980s had been met with a public outcry regarding safety, prompting successive State governments to be wary of the subject.
As Keralam draws up its 15th Plan, its power sector is in sharp focus. In recent months, the sector has been in the news over peak-hour electricity shortages and controversies over power purchase deals. At the same time, the State’s renewable capacity has risen from 572.42 MW in 2020-21 to 2382.34 MW in December 2025. Most of it is solar power, and much of that generated through household rooftop systems.
Energy, alongside higher education and employment generation form critical areas of the 15th Plan, Planning Board Vice-Chairman K.M. Chandrasekhar had said in a recent interview to The Hindu. Electricity is one area where the State will have to find large-scale investment, he said. According to the Approach Paper, the State’s ‘growth engine’ needs reliable power and preparations for ensuring long-term energy security should start now, since it would take more than five years to deliver results.

briefs.headline: Meritorious case eclipsed by form: Supreme Court steps in for school clerks after 20-year ordeal
briefs.bodyText: New Delhi: In a poignant reminder that justice can sometimes be derailed by technicalities, the Supreme Court has ordered a Mumbai school to pay Rs 10 lakh each as compensation to two former clerks whose services were terminated two decades ago, even as it acknowledged that their meritorious claims nearly failed due to poor drafting of legal papers. Prithviraj S Singh, a senior clerk (now deceased), and Shivadatta R Singh, a head clerk, were proceeded against by their school for alleged misappropriation of public money and allied charges under the Maharashtra Employees of Private Schools (Conditions of Service) Rules, 1981. An inquiry committee was constituted. The duo objected to one member, leading to a replacement; they objected again and then abstained in protest. The inquiry proceeded ex parte. Reports holding the charges established were never furnished to them before their termination. .After 47 years of legal battle, retired bank officer gets partial relief from Supreme Court. They approached the School Tribunal, which initially stayed the terminations. The school challenged this in the Bombay High Court. On March 17, 2005, a Single Judge passed a consent order substituting the interim relief that the employees would receive subsistence allowance, the school was at liberty to apply to lead evidence to substantiate the charges, and the Tribunal was to expedite the appeals. The school never led any evidence. The Tribunal, without insisting, dismissed the appeals in July 2006, relying on available documents and noting the employees’ non-participation. The clerks then filed writ petitions in the High Court, which focused largely on parity with the in-charge headmaster, who had received a lighter penalty of compulsory retirement. The petitions neither highlighted the school’s failure to lead evidence in terms of the consent order nor the non-supply of inquiry reports. A Single Judge dismissed their plea in 2016, distinguishing the headmaster’s case on grounds of length of service. .Unauthorised structures on National Highways: Drive to clear them must follow law, not bypass it: Supreme Court. Before the Supreme Court, the appellants’ arguments on the merits of the Tribunal’s orders were found to be beyond the pleadings. “A party is under obligation to plead its case by making the requisite averments/assertions in support of the relief that it claims, whereas a court is under no obligation to entertain a plea if the same is not supported by the necessary averments/assertions in the petition,” the court observed. Yet the bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu was struck by a deeper infirmity. “What, therefore, emerges is that there was no evidence worth the name before the tribunal resting whereon the charges against the appellants could be held ‘established’,” the November 18, 2026 judgment noted. The court held non-furnishing of the final inquiry reports was “a serious flaw.” An action contrary to an express judicial order “is a nullity and cannot be accepted.” The opening line of the judgment captured the tragedy, “The present case illustrates how a meritorious cause was allowed to fail by reason of inept drafting of a writ petition, the substance having been eclipsed by form.” Invoking Article 142 of the Constitution “ex debito justitiae,” the court directed the school to pay Rs 10 lakh to each appellant (or legal heirs of the deceased) within three months as full and final compensation for wrongful termination, with 12% interest on default. Larger relief might have followed had the petitions been properly framed, the court said, but that stage had passed. The order brings a measure of closure after years of litigation that outlived one of the appellants, underscoring both the limits of procedural justice and the Supreme Court’s residual power to do complete justice when form threatens to extinguish substance.

briefs.headline: Dual reporting structures built into the new police system in Bengaluru, raise concerns
briefs.deck: Speaking to The Hindu, senior officers who have previously held the position of Traffic DCPs in the city said the new hierarchy could create complications in obtaining approvals, planning, and coordinating with civic bodies
briefs.bodyText:
The restructuring of Bengaluru City Police into five commissionerates with a Chief Commissioner has several dual reporting structures built into it, which could potentially cause administrative issues, several senior police officials have flagged, on Wednesday following the government order on the restructuring. They have pointed out that hierarchy and chain of command was key in the police and that was not clear in the new organisational structure, even as roles are also yet to be defined properly.
For instance, the five police commissioners will directly report to the Director-General and Inspector-General of Police (DG&IGP), Karnataka, the order says, but while defining the role of the Chief Commissioner it said he would supervise the five commissioners. The order even acknowledges the confusion and says any clarification about mutual powers and functions of the Chief Commissioner of Police and Commissioners of Police of the five commissionerates will be clarified by the government for their smooth functioning. While the chain of command for the Law and Order functions of the police in the city remains clear, both traffic and crime seem to be marred by dual reporting structures that can cause confusion and put the lower bureaucracy under stress over conflicting orders and hamper a coherent strategy.
For the traffic police, the additional layer has created confusion for Deputy Commissioners of Police (DCPs), as they will now have to report to both the local commissioners and the Commissioner of Police (Traffic). Speaking to The Hindu, senior officers who have previously held the position of Traffic DCPs in the city said the new hierarchy could create complications in obtaining approvals, planning, and coordinating with civic bodies.
Currently, all planning functions of the Bengaluru Traffic Police fall under the ambit of the Joint Commissioner of Police. However, while the new order places the responsibility for planning city traffic with the Commissioner of Police (Traffic), there is no clarity on which aspects the Traffic DCPs will have to report to the local commissioners.
While each commissionerate has a DCP (Crime), there is also an Additional Commissioner (Anti-Rowdy Squad) at the city level, both of which are expected to replace the erstwhile Central Crime Branch. Hemanth M. Nimbalkar has also been tasked with “supervising crime control” across the city. This has also created a dual reporting structure for crime.
A senior police officer said the hierarchy could create pressure, with its effects cascading down to inspectors and lower-ranking officers.“For instance, if we have a case in hand and one officer suggests one method of investigation and another suggests a different one, which of the two should the DCP choose? This could further percolate down to the inspector if the pressure mounts on the DCP,” the officer explained.
Even local-level planning, including crime monitoring and patrolling strategies, could be affected by such conflicts, leading to a substantial burden on officers and delays in implementing plans, the officer said.

briefs.headline: Tamil Nadu Police launch e-CSR facility to enable online filing of complaints
briefs.deck: e-FIR facility for mobile phone, two-wheeler theft cases soon: DGP
briefs.bodyText:
The Tamil Nadu Director-General of Police and Head of Police Force, Mahesh Kumar Aggarwal, on Wednesday launched the e-CSR (electronic Community Service Register) facility at the State Police Headquarters here.
The initiative, aimed at making it easier for the public, particularly senior citizens and women, to lodge complaints online without having to visit police stations, is another step towards ensuring transparency in the police system, Dr. Aggarwal said.
“People are unhappy when their complaints are not acknowledged through the issuance of a CSR at police stations. They can now lodge complaints relating to minor offences online and receive an e-CSR on their mobile phones through SMS,” he said.
Complainants can approach the jurisdictional police station with the e-CSR and other relevant documents to obtain a regular CSR or have an FIR registered, as applicable, within three days.
Senior police officers would monitor the progress of e-CSR complaints and the number of cases subsequently converted into regular CSRs or FIRs. The e-FIR facility, introduced last month exclusively for cybercrime offences, had received a good response, he said.
e-FIR for mobile phone, two-wheeler thefts soon
Dr. Aggarwal said the e-FIR facility would soon be extended to cases involving missing or stolen mobile phones and two-wheelers.
Responding to a question on the possibility of misuse of the e-CSR facility, he said any such initiative could be misused. However, the police would proceed with further action only after establishing a prima facie case.
Zero tolerance towards custodial violence
Dr. Aggarwal said the Tamil Nadu Police had adopted a zero-tolerance policy towards custodial violence. The recent custodial death reported at the Chekkanoorani police station in Madurai district had been handed over to the Crime Branch-CID for investigation.
“We have instructed officials to ensure that people visiting police stations are covered by CCTV cameras at all times. Firm action will be taken wherever any lapse on the part of the police is established,” he said.
“Law and Order is being maintained well in the State. The average number of murders reported between January and November over the past five years stood at 1,421, while the figure had declined to 1,306 during the corresponding period this year,” he said.
Most murders were attributed to family disputes, illicit relationships and petty or verbal quarrels. Only 1% of the cases were linked to previous enmity involving rowdy elements, he said.
There had also been a significant increase in the registration of drug-related offences, seizure of contraband substances and the arrest of accused persons, he added.
Though the number of political agitations in Tamil Nadu increased by 35% compared with the previous year, there was no untoward incident since adequate bandobust arrangements were being made despite vacancies at various levels in the police force.
The Tamil Nadu Uniformed Services Recruitment Board had recently completed the recruitment of 3,000 police constables. The process of recruiting 1,200 Sub-Inspectors would also be completed soon. About 29,000 additional posts had been sanctioned to the police force by the Chief Minister, he said.

briefs.headline: Jayaprakash Narayan’s private secretary T. Abraham passes away
briefs.deck: Abraham’s biography titled Jayaprakash Narayanante Nizhalayi Oraal by Fr. Abraham Koshy Kunnumpurath, was released a few years ago
briefs.bodyText:
T. Abraham, who served as private secretary to Socialist stalwart Jayaprakash Narayan, passed away on Wednesday. He was 93. Abraham breathed his last at his residence at Mavelikkara.
He had also served as public relations officer with the Tata group.
He is survived by his wife Ammini Abraham and children Mini Jacob, Prakash, and Prabhash. The funeral prayers will be conducted at his residence at 10 a.m. on Friday, followed by the funeral service at 11 a.m. at St. Mary’s Orthodox Church (Muttel Church), Kuttamperoor.
Condoling his death, Varughese George, secretary general of RJD, remembered that Abraham had served as private secretary to JP from the Sarvodaya period to the post-Emergency days.
Abraham’s biography titled Jayaprakash Narayanante Nizhalayi Oraal by Fr. Abraham Koshy Kunnumpurath, was released a few years ago.

briefs.headline: Punjab bridge collapses on Patiala-Sangrur road, two trucks plunge into canal
briefs.deck: An iron bridge over the Bhakra Canal in Punjab collapsed with two trucks on it, which fell into the structure. One of the trucks caught fire shortly after the collapse, resulting in emergency response efforts. Fire brigade personnel worked swiftly to control the blaze and prevent further spread of the fire. Police teams arrived at the scene to manage the situation as onlookers gathered around the…
briefs.bodyText:
PATIALA: An iron bridge over the Bhakra Canal in Punjab collapsed while two trucks were crossing it early Thursday, sending both vehicles into the damaged structure. One of the trucks caught fire soon after the collapse.
The incident took place near Pasiana village on the Patiala-Sangrur Bypass. No casualties have been reported so far, according to preliminary information.
Fire brigade personnel rushed to the spot and battled the blaze before bringing it under control. Police teams also reached the site to handle the situation as crowds gathered around the damaged bridge.
It is not yet clear what caused the structure to collapse. The incident is expected to disrupt traffic on the Patiala-Sangrur Bypass.
(With inputs from PTI)

briefs.headline: Cummins under pressure as Bancroft's claims trigger calls for captaincy review
briefs.deck: Cameron Bancroft's recent statements have raised serious doubts regarding Pat Cummins's credibility as Test captain. Bancroft revealed that many team members knew about the ball-tampering plot during the 2018 South Africa tour. Cummins has consistently denied any knowledge of the incident, despite the mounting public scrutiny. An independent forum has been established by Cricket Australia for…
briefs.bodyText:
Australia captain 
Pat Cummins
 is facing mounting pressure over his leadership following 
Cameron Bancroft
's explosive revelations about the 2018 ball-tampering scandal, with calls growing for an immediate review of his position as Test skipper.
Bancroft, who was banned for nine months for his role in the infamous 'Sandpapergate' scandal, has questioned Cummins' credibility over his repeated denials of knowledge of the ball-tampering plot, claiming the captain's recent comments were the "final straw" that prompted him to break his silence.
The 33-year-old also revealed that speaking publicly about the incident had left him feeling relieved and liberated after carrying the burden for years. In an explosive 4,497-word column published on Wednesday, Bancroft reiterated claims that the wider Australian team was aware of the plan to tamper with the ball during the 2018 South Africa tour.
"Obviously, yeah, I’ve been carrying a lot of this stuff for a long period of time," Bancroft said after releasing his account, as per 9News in Perth.
"So I feel really freed and really happy to be able to do that. And obviously now there’s a process in place which Cricket Australia have put in (forum). 
Yeah, I look forward to being a part of that process," he added.
Cummins' denial comes under fresh scrutiny
Cummins, however, has stood firm on his position that he had no knowledge of the ball-tampering plan, maintaining that his account of the events has remained consistent over the past eight years.
His manager Neil Maxwell issued a statement reiterating the Australian captain's stance, while expressing sympathy for Bancroft.
"Pat's position hasn't changed in eight years. He's been consistent and adamant from day one," Maxwell said.
"Pat feels for Cam (Bancroft) of course. He has been through a lot. We would urge people to again read Pat's interview transcript. There is nothing he hasn't answered. And that includes in response to what Cam has now said."
The developments have nevertheless intensified scrutiny of Cummins' leadership, with prominent Australian cricket writer Robert Craddock calling for an immediate review of his captaincy.
"Pat Cummins' future as test captain should be placed under immediate review after Cameron Bancroft's stunning accusation that the skipper didn't tell us the truth," Craddock wrote in The Australian.
The growing controversy has also prompted questions across Australian media about whether Cummins can continue as Test captain amid the renewed scrutiny surrounding the scandal.
Bancroft's account reopens old wounds
In his latest account, Bancroft acknowledged that 
David Warner
 had raised the idea of using sandpaper on the ball to generate reverse swing during the second Test against South Africa in Port Elizabeth in 2018.
The discussion reportedly took place during the tea break on Day 2, in the presence of bowling coach David Saker and then head coach Darren Lehmann.
The revelations have reopened wounds from the Cape Town Test, where Bancroft was caught using sandpaper on the ball. The incident resulted in lengthy bans for Bancroft, Warner and then-captain Steve Smith, who was also stripped of the captaincy.
The controversy resurfaced following Usman Khawaja's allegations in his autobiography that the wider team knew about the plan and should collectively accept responsibility. Warner and former Australia pacer Chadd Sayers have also backed Khawaja's account, adding to the pressure on Cricket Australia (CA).
CA's 2018 investigation had concluded that the conspiracy was limited to the three players who were punished.
Cricket Australia opens independent forum
Amid the renewed controversy, CA chief executive Todd Greenberg announced the establishment of an independent forum to allow players to share their accounts of the scandal.
However, Greenberg made it clear that the governing body was not looking to reopen the investigation or impose fresh sanctions.
"Looking for the perfect truth doesn't exist, and we're not chasing that," Greenberg told reporters on Wednesday.
Former Australia opener Warner, meanwhile, appeared reluctant to revisit the episode, saying he had nothing further to add when asked whether he would participate in the forum.
"At the end of the day, we owned what we did. So we can't do any more," Warner told the media in Sydney.
Sayers was also uncertain about participating, questioning the usefulness of a process that might not make the complete accounts public.
"What's the point ... if there's certain bits that they want to cut out," he told local radio station SEN on Thursday.
With Bancroft now willing to participate in CA's independent process and fresh questions being raised about what the wider group knew, Sandpapergate has once again become a major issue for Australian cricket. For Cummins, whose denial remains unchanged, the controversy has evolved into an increasingly uncomfortable test of his leadership.

stories.headline: Heritage walk at Bengaluru’s Someshwara temple celebrates local history
stories.deck: This heritage walk through the centuries-old temple, a recent collaboration between Chai with History and Yellow Veranda Experiences, seeks to bring the past alive for its participants
stories.bodyText:
“This temple is literally the entrance to Bengaluru,” announces public archaeologist Lathashree KS, pointing to the Someshwara Swamy Temple in Ulsoor, where we have gathered on a pleasant Saturday morning. Over the chants wafting from the temple, which is adorned with a sky-grazing Vijayanagara-style gopuram, she explains why the area is important: “The highway to Kolar and Chintamani is here, and traders coming from there to go to the city market beyond have to pass through here. This is the first area you enter when you come to the city after trading with your ox carts and camels,” she says.
It wasn’t just traders and their animals who stopped here to rest after an arduous journey, says Lathashree, who founded Chai with History, an informal archaeology and history group in Bengaluru, in 2013. “It is not surprising that the Madras Sappers came and set up a cantonment here,” she elaborates as we begin our heritage walk through the centuries-old temple.
Over the next couple of hours, we traverse the temple’s impressive open mantapa with its carved pillars and its beautiful sculpted panels, peaceful inner sanctum and surrounding shrines, learning about its mythologies and histories along the way.
For instance, a sculpture of a Shuka Bhashini, a lady conversing with a parrot, bears a tiny signature of the sculptor: a little squirrel. “He didn’t have to do that, but we can see how the artist observed nature, although he was carving for a temple, under strictures,” she says. Other interesting learnings include how Lord Cornwallis, who led the British troops in the final Anglo-Mysorean War, camped here with them; why the oldest part of the temple lies at its very centre; how the interconnectedness of nature and human beings, apparent in some of the sculptures, is a crucial aspect of Shavisim; and that the entire temple was built out of local granite. “It is a people’s temple,” says Lathashree.
The walk through this people’s temple, one of the two events regularly conducted as part of a recent collaboration with Yellow Veranda Experiences — the other is a Brahmi script workshop, ending with a Mauryan meal — is the latest offering of Chai with History, which has evolved considerably since its genesis 13 years ago.
“It started randomly,” says Lathashree, pointing out that since she holds an MA in archaeology and indology from Deccan College, Pune, people started reaching out to her on Facebook with questions. “I started providing information,” she says. Soon, a member of a Facebook group suggested meeting regularly to discuss history. “I agreed to meet up once every month.”
A motley bunch of people began meeting every month, congregating around the benches at the Government Museum on Kasturba Road. “We made it our adda. And a small canteen made better tea than coffee, so we called it Chai with History,” she recalls.
Gradually, generic history conversations became more specific, focusing on a variety of topics, including the Mauryan Dynasty, epigraphy, how to read sculptures, the Jataka Tales and stratigraphy. Even during the pandemic, Chai with History continued in an online format, with sessions continuing until 2023, when Lathashree took a step back for personal reasons, she says.
Earlier this year, however, she restarted it, with Chai with History now conducted in four major formats: Shared Space, for discussions about the history behind a particular hobby such as pottery, philately or poetry; Cosy Conversations, for curated conversations with a small group; Idea Lounge, for interaction on books and other readings, especially for those new to history; and Walks and Workshops, for heritage walks and focused workshops, like the one we are currently attending, as part of the collaboration with Yellow Veranda Experiences.
According to Soumya Jayaraj, the founder of Yellow Veranda Experiences, which is located in Sthala, a heritage space in Ulsoor, “We thought we would curate unique experiences around these spaces that are rich in history and heritage,” she says. This led to collaborations with experts such as Lathashree. “We were interested in the Someshwara Temple for its history and its iconography. We enjoy incorporating such subjects into our heritage experiences,” she says of the walk, which ended with a hot South Indian breakfast and excellent coffee, throughly enjoyed by the small, ecclectic group of people who attended the experience.
One of them is senior plant biologist R. Ganesan. This walk, he says, made him think about how the city’s botanical history is tied to historical events, whether it was Kempe Gowda, the Mughals, Hyder Ali, Tipu Sultan or the British. “It was a learning to hear about the development of Bangalore and how the temples store the information and chronicle it,” says Ganesan, an adjunct fellow at Ashoka Trust for Research in Ecology and the Environment (ATREE),
Another participant, Meghana Laxman Patgar, a city-based content creator who runs the Instagram page Yo Bengaluru, is also impressed with Lathashree’s knowledge and patience. “She explained everything beautifully, answering every question and doubt, and also allowed people to share their stories,” she says.
Besides helping spread awareness about history, Lathashree feels these sessions also nudge us to think about who we are and where we came from. She recalls a moment as a student when she held a million-year-old hand axe and realised how that object connected her to someone, not even a modern human, who inhabited this world all those years ago. “It was a moment when the past became sacred. That is what I want them to understand.”

The driver reportedly lost control while attempting to overtake another vehicle. Local police confirmed that…
stories.bodyText:
CHIKKABALLAPUR: At least four people were killed and another was injured after a car collided with a goods vehicle on a highway in Karnataka’s Chikkaballapur district on Wednesday evening.
The car, which had five occupants, was heading towards Hyderabad from Bengaluru when the accident took place between 5.30pm and 6pm.
All five occupants were neighbours from Old Yelahanka in Bengaluru.
According to a preliminary investigation, the car driver allegedly tried to overtake another vehicle, lost control and crossed the road divider before entering the opposite carriageway and crashing into the goods vehicle, a senior police officer said.

stories.headline: GTA 6 is out, but this Bengaluru’s flyover isn’t: City's ‘Stonehenge’, 9 years in the making, misses another deadline
stories.deck: Bengaluru's Ejipura flyover project continues to see delays despite having been started nearly nine years ago. Originally scheduled for completion in November 2019, several challenges have stalled progress over the years. After changing contractors, current obstacles include further land acquisition and community objections related to tree removal. The project remains incomplete with multiple…
stories.bodyText:
BENGALURU: Bengaluru's much-delayed Ejipura flyover, dubbed the city's 'Stonehenge' for its years of stalled construction and unfinished pillars, is staring at yet another deadline miss.
Nearly nine years after work began, the 2.5km elevated corridor may not be ready even by December-end, prolonging commuters' wait for relief along the busy Koramangala–Ejipura–Madiwala stretch.
Originally scheduled for completion in November 2019, the project has endured repeated deadline extensions, contractor failure, failed tenders, land acquisition hurdles, delayed clearances and disputes over payments.
Despite a change of contractor and several assurances from civic authorities, the flyover remains unfinished.
From 2017 to 2022: Simplex fails to complete the project
The flyover was originally awarded to Kolkata-based Simplex Infrastructure Ltd in 2017, with an estimated project cost of Rs 158 crore. BBMP issued the work order on May 4, 2017, and the project was scheduled for completion by November 2019.
However, construction faced problems from the beginning. Delays in traffic police clearances, permission for controlled blasting and land acquisition affected the pace of work.
By 2020, BBMP was still struggling to acquire portions of land required for the flyover, including property belonging to St John's Hospital, the Central Public Works Department and the Indian Institute of Astrophysics.
The Covid-19 pandemic further affected labour mobilisation in 2020.
Despite repeated deadline extensions, Simplex failed to complete the project. The company was facing financial difficulties, and construction eventually ground to a halt.
A public interest litigation filed in 2021 brought the matter before the Karnataka high court. Following judicial intervention, BBMP terminated Simplex's contract in March 2022.
By then, the civic body had spent around Rs 75 crore on the project. It also forfeited the contractor's security deposit of Rs 10.16 crore and imposed a penalty of around Rs 2.5 crore.
Three failed tenders before BSCPL took over
Finding a replacement contractor proved equally difficult.
BBMP floated a fresh tender in August 2022, but the process was recalled. Another tender, floated in January 2023 for Rs 144 crore, attracted only one bidder, Hyderabad-based BSCPL Infrastructure Ltd, which quoted around Rs 205 crore, approximately 44% above the estimated amount.
The bid did not receive financial approval, forcing BBMP to cancel the tender in February 2023.
After revising the estimates and introducing a price-adjustment clause, BBMP eventually awarded the remaining work to BSCPL Infrastructure Ltd in November 2023, with a 15-month completion deadline.
The cost of completing the remaining construction was pegged at Rs 176.1 crore, excluding GST.
However, the change in contractor did not immediately accelerate the project.
BSCPL flagged delays in land acquisition, mobilisation payments and access to the casting yard. The company also had to obtain an Indian Institute of Science (IISc) assessment of the structure built by Simplex before proceeding with further construction.
The assessment was completed in May 2024, several months after the new contractor took over.
BBMP also issued notices to BSCPL over slow progress and imposed a penalty of Rs 25 lakh.
Land acquisition, trees and ramps become fresh hurdles
Even as construction picked up in 2025, land acquisition near St John's Medical College Hospital continued to affect the construction of ramps.
The project also faced objections from residents over BBMP's proposal to remove 157 trees along Koramangala's 100 Feet Road. More than 150 objections and suggestions were received before the deadline for public submissions in January 2025.
Residents suggested changes to the ramp design and alignment to save trees, while activists questioned the changing number of trees proposed for removal.
In January 2026, GBA chief commissioner M Maheshwar Rao directed officials to mark the land required at St John's Hospital and begin construction of five portal piers. Hospital management agreed to allow temporary use of a portion of its land along the compound wall.
Officials were directed to install barricades and rebuild the compound wall after construction.
The administration subsequently announced fresh completion targets, but the project continued to miss them.
Why December-end is also looking difficult
The project has already seen its completion targets move from November 2019 to 2020, December 2021, 2025 and multiple dates in 2026.
The main elevated corridor still has pending construction and finishing work, including ramps, pavement, crash barriers, drainage, lighting, lane markings and road signage.
The additional entry and exit ramps towards Sarjapur Road also require further land acquisition and may take longer to complete.
For commuters, the concern is no longer just when the flyover will be inaugurated, but whether the entire project will finally be completed after years of disruption.
"GTA 6 is getting released yet Ejipura flyover couldn't get be operational yet," a social media user posted, summing up the frustration surrounding the project.

stories.headline: Bengaluru is India’s AI, start-up capital; city captures 47% of national venture funding: Report
stories.deck: The city is now the world’s fifth-largest unicorn hub, the largest outside the U.S., Europe, China, and London,with 57 unicorns valued at $211 billion, representing 55.3% of the combined value of all Indian unicorns
stories.bodyText:
City-based start-ups have raised about $85 billion since 2010, 47% of all venture funding raised by Indian start-ups, with $76.5 billion of it in the past 10 years.
This milestone was revealed in the Bengaluru Innovation Report 2026, released on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) by Karnataka’s Minister for Home, Electronics, IT & BT, Priyank M. Kharge, during the second day of the Bengaluru Tech Summit 2026.
Prepared by the Karnataka Digital Economy Mission (KDEM) and 3one4 Capital, using Tracxn data, the report highlights the city’s evolution into a global deep-tech powerhouse.
According to the findings, Bengaluru is unequivocally India’s Artificial Intelligence capital, commanding 36.3% of the country’s native AI start-up funding and housing 71% of India’s AI and deep-tech unicorns created since 2023. Out of 1,556 deep-tech startups founded in the city since 2010, 1,319 are active and funded, raising $3.77 billion. Women entrepreneurs are also driving this wave, with nearly 30% of India’s active, funded women-led deep-tech and AI start-ups originating in the city, raising $323.65 million.
The city’s wealth creation metrics remain unmatched nationally. Bengaluru is now the world’s fifth-largest unicorn hub, and the largest outside the U.S., Europe, China, and London, with 57 unicorns valued at $211 billion, representing 55.3% of the combined value of all Indian unicorns.
Further, as per the report, it leads the nation with 212 “soonicorns” (soon-to-be unicorns). Start-ups here scale faster than anywhere else in India, reaching unicorn status in six years and public exits in 8.2 years, beating the global exit average of 11.1 years. Since November 2024, 16 Bengaluru-linked companies have gone public with a combined listing value of $42 billion.
Mr. Kharge emphasised on expanding this success across the State. “The Bengaluru Innovation Report 2026 shows how far Karnataka’s founders have come and how much more they can build from here. Our next task is to make sure a world-class AI, quantum or semiconductor company can grow just as well in Kalaburagi, Hubballi or Mangaluru. Deep tech rewards patience, and Karnataka will stay the course,’’ he stated.
The State is backing this vision with aggressive regional initiatives, including the ₹1,000 crore Local Economy Accelerator Programme (LEAP), Global Technology Centres in Mysuru, Hubballi, and Belagavi, and the ELEVATE grant programme, which has already supported 1,479 start-ups across 30 districts.
Highlighting the ecosystem’s investor appeal, KDEM chairman B.V. Naidu, a key architect of Karnataka’s IT industry, noted, “This report gives investors, GCCs and founders a data-backed view of what Karnataka, Bengaluru and our emerging clusters, offers.’’
Through the Beyond Bengaluru Mission, BLUE investor days and the Cluster Seed Fund, KDEM would keep connecting capital and companies with talent across the State, Mr. Naidu added.
KEONICS chairman Sharath Bachegowda concluded that through continued investments in infrastructure and talent, the state aims to build an ecosystem where enterprises “can innovate, scale and compete globally”.
Industry and government leaders echoed the shift toward homegrown capital, noting that 52% of Alternative Investment Fund (AIF) capital now comes from domestic investors. “With 36.3% of India’s native AI funding already in Bengaluru, the next decade belongs to founders building hard technology for the world from Karnataka,” opined Prashant Prakash, chairman of Karnataka’s Vision Group on Startups.
Manjula N, secretary of the Department of Electronics, IT, BT and S&T said, the State’s focus is now on “converting early support into scale: government as a first customer, patient capital for deep tech, and research that moves from our laboratories into the market”.

briefs.headline: Proof submitted, Karnataka urges Centre to review E20 rule
briefs.deck: Karnataka has sent an official appeal to the Centre urging a thorough re-evaluation of the E20 programme for ethanol blending. The state has raised alarming concerns about petrol samples revealing ethanol levels exceeding 31%, which poses potential safety hazards. State officials are calling for robust infrastructure to support this blending initiative, emphasizing the importance of collective…
briefs.bodyText:
BENGALURU: 
Karnataka
 has asked Centre to review its E20 programme in consultation with states, backing its plea with lab tests that allegedly found excess ethanol in petrol samples.
In a letter to Union petroleum minister 
Hardeep Singh Puri
 Wednesday, food, civil supplies and consumer affairs minister Rizwan Arshad said the state was not against ethanol blending but opposed over-blending.
“The ethanol blending programme cannot come at the cost of citizens. A transition of this scale needs the whole ecosystem to be ready, including fuel infrastructure and ethanol-compliant vehicles, and that takes time,” he said.
-
In his letter, he states officials inspected 63 IOCL, BPCL, HPCL and MRPL outlets in Sept. Samples went to labs of three public sector oil marketing companies (OMCs), which have so far sent reports for only 42, none stating ethanol content. OMCs told the state that research octane number was the compliance parameter, though they acknowledged that IS 17021 mandates measuring ethanol content. No reason was given for the delay in the remaining 21 reports.
OMCs also questioned the sampling procedure and density. The state rejected this, saying officials followed Clause 8 of the Motor Spirit and High-Speed Diesel Order, 2005, and handed over sealed counterpart samples on the spot.
Fresh samples sent to NABL-accredited labs showed wide variation. “Of 14 samples tested, 11 had more than 20% ethanol, the highest at over 31%,” Arshad said. The lowest was 13.5%. High ethanol was also found in premium petrol sold at Rs 120 to Rs 140 a litre.
Arshad said inspections appeared to have had a deterrent effect and the blend may have since been corrected, but continuous checks were needed.
He also opposed two central notifications on fuel dispensers. The first, dated Dec 18, 2025, doubled verification intervals from 12 to 24 months. The second, dated May 8, 2026, let private govt-approved centres verify dispensers, a job earlier done by govt inspectors. A legal metrology survey found 101 outlets dispensing fuel beyond the permissible error.
Arshad said E20 needed urgent “course correction”, with adequate time and support to upgrade vehicles, fuel infrastructure, dispensers, storage and testing facilities. “Karnataka has placed all its evidence before the Govt of India and would welcome a detailed discussion at the earliest, so that together we can protect the people and restore public trust,” he said.
Meanwhile, senior BJP functionary and former minister Murugesh R Nirani dismissed Arshad’s claim that petrol samples contained up to 31.2% ethanol, alleging that the testing methodology was flawed. He said sampling should involve representatives of fuel outlets, oil marketing companies, the state food and civil supplies department and Union govt. He also rejected claims that ethanol blending was intended to benefit Union minister Nitin Gadkari’s companies, revealing his own company produced 28 lakh litres of ethanol daily against Gadkari’s company’s two lakh litres.
Karnataka’s key demands
*Keep E10 and ethanol-free petrol available at affordable prices till vehicles are compatible
*Create E20 compensation fund for vehicles damaged by petrol above the prescribed limit

briefs.headline: Bengaluru City Police restructured; five Commissioners and a Chief Commissioner appointed
briefs.deck: R. Hithendra appointed the new Chief Commissioner of Bengaluru City Police
briefs.bodyText:
The Karnataka government on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) restructured the Bengaluru City Police, creating five police commissionerates — Central, North, East, South and West and appointed a Chief Commissioner to oversee the five commissionerates, aping the Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) and five city corporations model.
The Karnataka Cabinet on October 6 approved the five commissionerate model for restructuring of the city police. A Government Order issued on Wednesday, said the restructuring aims to streamline policing, strengthen administrative supervision and improve law and order across the rapidly expanding city.
Additional Director-General of Police (ADGP) R. Hithendra, a 1996-batch IPS officer, has been posted as the new Chief Commissioner, Bengaluru City, replacing Seemant Kumar Singh.
Another ADGP rank-officer Hemanth M. Nimbalkar has been posted as Commissioner (Traffic), Bengaluru City, and given concurrent charge of Commissioner (Anti Rowdy Squad).
The five new commissionerates will work as independent units with Deputy Commmissioners for Law and Order, Traffic and Crime units. These commissionerates will also have their own City Armed Reserve (CAR) units, women and cyber crime police stations.
These commissionerates will be led by Inspector-General of Police (IGP) rank officers — Labhu Ram for Central, P.S. Harsha for East, Vikash Kumar Vikash for West, and M.B. Boralingaiah for North. C. Vamsi Krishna, a Deputy Inspector General (DIG) rank officer has been posted as Joint Commissioner (Administration) and given concurrent charge of the South Commissionerate.
The new Bengaluru Police jurisdiction has been expanded to include seven new police stations, including Sarjapur, Bannerghatta and Anekal, mostly in the south-eastern parts of the city. The government has also created four new divisions - three law and order divisions of Indiranagar, Gandhinagar and Peenya apart from a new Central Traffic Division.

briefs.headline: Loans, long hours and little pay: ASHA workers give reality check in Bengaluru
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru: Sharanamma, an ASHA worker from Afzalpur taluk in Kalaburagi, sat under the scorching afternoon sun at Freedom Park Wednesday, determined not to leave until govt agreed to her demand for a monthly honorarium of Rs 15,000.
In her 40s, she is the sole breadwinner of a family with two mentally challenged sons, aged 18 and 25. Having worked as an ASHA worker for 15 years, she has lost count of the homes she has visited and childbirths she has assisted. But the meagre pay has made supporting her family increasingly difficult. “I was being paid Rs 3,500 when I started work. Then after many rounds of protest where we braved rain and cold, it was raised to Rs 5,000. I have no support from my family. I have undergone great difficulty over the years to even afford treatment for my sons,” said Sharanamma.
Her story echoes those of thousands of ASHA workers protesting at Freedom Park since Tuesday, demanding better remuneration and working conditions.
Many say they were initially told they would have to work only 2.5 hours a day when they joined 10-15 years ago. Today, they spend six to seven hours on duties ranging from monitoring pregnancies and vaccinations to tracking disease outbreaks and conducting door-to-door screenings under the Gruha Arogya scheme.
Shobha, an ASHA worker from GBA area
“It is not just hours. In a city like Bengaluru, we have to climb flights of stairs in every building every time they want us to conduct a survey. All we are taking home from this job is extreme body pain. We don’t get benefits like PF. Our families do not even get medical benefits and least of all, even our salaries are not regular,” said Shobha, an ASHA worker from the GBA area.
The workers spent Tuesday night at Freedom Park, braving the cold. Many of them also developed fever and stomach infections. “I have been doing this for 18 years now. If they had told us back then only that is all we would get, I would have quit and done something else. Now, I will not move from here until they fix Rs 15,000 as our honorarium. We have come ready with bed sheets and blankets. We will stay here as long as it takes,” said Parvathi, an ASHA worker from Kollegala in Chamarajanagar.
Nirmala, an ASHA worker from Chamarajnagar
Nirmala, another ASHA worker from Chamarajanagar, added, “Our lives are running on loans. The Rs 5,000 we get goes in paying interest for the loans. How are we supposed to ever make savings?”
Health minister UT Khader’s assurance that he would discuss their demands with chief minister 
DK Shivakumar
 failed to persuade them to withdraw the protest. The workers are now looking to Thursday’s cabinet meeting for concrete assurances.
Inset: Ravi Kumar slams govt over ASHA protest
Chief Whip of the Opposition in the legislative council N Ravi Kumar Wednesday termed the state govt’s attitude towards protesting ASHA workers “insensitive and inhuman.” He said their demand to raise the monthly honorarium from Rs 5,000 to Rs 15,000 was legitimate and criticised ministers for not visiting the protesters.

briefs.headline: Switchgear factory to turn into museum of innovation & tech in Bengaluru
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru
: The architectural model of the country’s first Museum of Innovation, Startup and Technology (MIST), which will showcase India’s technological and entrepreneurial journey, was unveiled at the Bengaluru Tech Summit-2026 being held here.
The design, conceptualised by a consortium led by Heneghan Peng Architects (the firm behind Cairo’s Grand Egyptian Museum), was selected through a two-stage global competition launched in January 2026, which attracted 13 consortiums comprising 30 Indian and international firms. The first phase of the ambitious project, which will come up at the NGEF premises in the city’s Baiyappanahalli area, is likely to become operational in 2028.
MIST is being developed as a public-private partnership between UnboxingBLR (51% stake) and the Karnataka govt (49%) through the Karnataka Technology Innovation Museum Foundation (KTIMF).
Speaking at the unveiling, Prashanth Prakash, chairperson of KTIMF and UnboxingBLR, said: “India’s innovation story is being written every day in labs, garages and startup offices across the country, but much of it goes unrecorded. 
MIST is our effort to change that. By turning a historic NGEF factory shed into India’s first museum of modern innovation, technology and entrepreneurship, we want to build a world-class institution that preserves, celebrates and inspires innovation.” He said the pavilion was a first look at the vision and invited the wider innovation ecosystem to help shape the museum.
Manjula N, secretary (dept of IT and BT, science and technology), said: “MIST shows our belief that public-private collaboration can create lasting public infrastructure. Turning the NGEF campus, with its industrial heritage and urban forest, into a home for innovation shows how Bengaluru can honour its past while building its future.”
From health to electronics and many more
The museum will showcase innovation in India since 1947, across aerospace, healthcare, consumer products, edtech, energy, telecom, AI and more. Its key themes will include digital public infrastructure, biotechnology, space, startups, AI and deep tech. The team said the aim is to reveal the prototypes and early designs behind technologies like electric vehicles and mobile phones, which the public has never had access to. The project is expected to serve as an immersive educational and cultural space, making technology accessible to students, researchers and the general public, and to inspire young people from schools and universities to lead innovation.
Old factory reuse
The museum will come up on the 105-acre NGEF campus. It will occupy a disused switchgear factory shed that, members of the project said, shut down in 2001. Through adaptive reuse of the existing 10,061sqm structure, the project will expand to nearly 24,000sqm, of which around 12,325sqm will be dedicated to the museum.
Axonometric view of galleries
The design of the galleries in the museum will be guided by two concepts. The first, “forests and machines,” reflects the campus’s urban forest and industrial past. The second, “expansion and disruption,” means the museum will not look the same for long: the whole space will evolve every few hours so that visitors do not feel bored or fatigued. 
At certain intervals, the exhibits will be dimmed and projection mapping will create an entirely new environment. They added that exhibits will be interactive, experiential and gamified, rather than the press-a-button format of traditional science museums.
Not a tree will be cut
The museum will come up on the 105-acre NGEF campus, which has 65 acres of green cover. Members of the project said the architects were given a clear brief: not a single tree should be cut. The existing structure will be retained, with only the facade changed and the interiors reworked so that the space is sustainable and regenerative.

briefs.headline: Print kiosks target last-minute college rush in Bengaluru
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru
: Visualise this: A seminar is set to begin in 10 minutes. The presentation is ready, but the handout is still on a phone. For students facing that familiar scramble, an ATM-like print kiosk on campus could make the difference between a quick print and a dash to a photocopy shop.
In fact, a model of the print kiosk was showcased at the summit by Chennai-based startup QwikPrint, which has completed test runs by installing self-service print kiosks at colleges and public institutions across Bengaluru and 
Karnataka
. The machine lets users upload a document, select print settings, pay digitally and collect the pages using a code.
The company maintained that it has installed the kiosk at St Joseph’s University, PES University and Sairam College in the city. A kiosk has six paper trays and can hold up to 2,000 sheets across paper types, including A4, A3 and bond paper, it says. The machines are also available at outlets in Hebbal. A kiosk has been installed on the Mysuru District Court campus, said Aadhithya M, an associate at QwikPrint.
“Currently, we have 85 such kiosks installed across India. Bengaluru is among the top cities adapting to it,” Aadhithya said. The company says colleges can set their own prices: an 80-gsm sheet costs it about Rs 1 and may be sold for Rs 3 or more. Installation costs institutions between Rs 1.5 lakh and Rs 3 lakh, depending on expected workload.

briefs.headline: Greater Bengaluru Authority announces Special Summary Revision schedule; final voter list on Jan 20
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru: The Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) has announced the schedule for the Special Summary Revision (SSR) of electoral rolls, following directions from the 
Election Commission of India
 (ECI). The exercise will continue until Jan 20, 2027, when the final electoral rolls are scheduled to be published.
As part of the exercise, the rationalisation and rearrangement of polling stations are expected to be completed by Nov 23. The integrated draft electoral rolls will be published on De 1. Claims and objections can be filed between Dec 1 and 31, and will be disposed of by Jan 14. The qualifying date for the revision is Jan 1, 2027.
The announcement comes amid uncertainty over which electoral rolls will be used for the GBA elections. The State Election Commission (SEC) is awaiting directions from the 
Supreme Court
 on whether it can use the existing pre-SIR ward-wise rolls or the final post-SIR Assembly rolls published on Oct 27.
The SEC had approached the Supreme Court seeking clarity on the issue and a revised timeline for the elections. This followed delays by the ECI in furnishing the final post-SIR voter data in the required format to prepare ward-wise electoral rolls.
The SEC, however, has said that the routine revision will not affect the GBA election schedule.

briefs.headline: Model start-up parks on 1,000 acres near Bengaluru, Hubballi-Dharwad on the anvil: M.B. Patil
briefs.deck: Mr. Patil said some start-up founders had pointed out that land prices in Bengaluru had risen sharply and making land available at affordable rates would greatly benefit them.
briefs.bodyText:
The State government is planning to set up model start-up parks spread across 1,000 acres near Bengaluru and 100 to 200 acres near Hubballi-Dharwad to further strengthen the start-up ecosystem in Karnataka, said Large and Medium Industries Minister M.B. Patil here on Wednesday (November 18, 2026).
Speaking to the press after an interactive session with start-up founders and investors at the Bengaluru Tech Summit, Mr. Patil said some start-up founders had pointed out that land prices in Bengaluru had risen sharply and making land available at affordable rates would greatly benefit them.
To address this concern of start-up entrepreneurs, Mr. Patil said his government would consider setting up start-up parks in the State. The next steps would be decided after examining the various ways in which the necessary support could be extended, he added.
Some start-up founders who were part of the interaction said there are more than 200 electric two-wheeler manufacturers in the country. Of these, four companies sell more than 100 vehicles a month, and all four have their design operations in Bengaluru. However, three of them manufacture their vehicles outside Karnataka, while only one has a manufacturing facility in the State. Some start-up founders attributed this to the lack of affordable land.
Responding to their concerns, Mr. Patil promised them that his government would work towards establishing dedicated start-up parks. “The government was aware that it would be difficult for entrepreneurs to bear the entire investment burden on their own. We will examine the possibility of allotting industrial plots in the proposed start-up parks under a lease-cum-sale arrangement or through other suitable mechanisms,’’ the Minister said.
He also said the government would consider providing an additional 5% subsidy to start-ups located beyond Bengaluru, over and above the assistance currently available.
According to Mr. Patil, the government aims to bring more than 130 services under the single-window clearance system. Of these, 116 services are already available, while the remaining 10-15 services are expected to be brought under its ambit within a month. “Steps will be taken to ensure that the single-window system functions effectively in the true sense,’’ he said, also stressing the need to revise the curricula of technical education institutions in line with industry requirements.
Prashanth Prakash, chairman of the Karnataka government’s Vision Group on Startups, said the State had a strong ecosystem for start-ups. He urged entrepreneurs to look beyond design and manufacturing and also take up the production of machinery and equipment required for manufacturing activities within Karnataka. This would help reduce costs, he emphasised.

stories.headline: Oil prices slip as supply concerns and US rate hike fears weigh on market sentiment
stories.deck: Recent fluctuations in oil prices have been attributed to growing supply expectations and uneasiness over interest rates. However, these decreases faced limitations due to escalating tensions in the Strait of Hormuz, where attacks on shipping have emerged. Moreover, US crude inventories rose significantly beyond predictions, intensifying a cautious sentiment in oil markets.
stories.bodyText:
Oil prices edged lower on Thursday, with both major benchmarks trading in the red as expectations of higher supplies and interest rates continued to weigh on the market. Concerns over attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz amid the ongoing Iran war provided some support, limiting the decline.
WTI crude futures were trading at $82.92 a barrel, down 34 cents, or 0.41%, while Brent crude stood at $91.93, slipping 2 cents, or 0.02%.
The two benchmarks had ended the previous session lower. Brent lost 1.3%, while WTI declined 3.2%, touching its lowest level since August 26. The fall came amid growing expectations of excess supply, with crude shipments through the Strait of Hormuz recovering to levels seen before the war.
The possibility of another US interest rate increase has added to the cautious mood in oil markets. Higher borrowing costs could weigh on economic growth and slow the expansion in oil demand. A stronger dollar could further add to the pressure by making crude, which is priced in dollars, more expensive for buyers using other currencies.
Minutes of the US Federal Reserve's October meeting, published on Wednesday, reinforced expectations among investors that the central bank could increase interest rates at its December meeting to bring inflation under control.
"Softer oil prices provide some relief to those concerned about persistent inflationary pressures, although the question is no longer simply whether the Fed will hike rates in December, but by how much. This, in turn, supports the dollar, hindering any attempt by the oil market to rally," analysts at PVM, a brokerage, said in a note dated November 18.
The supply outlook also came under pressure after US crude inventories posted a sharper-than-anticipated increase.
The US Energy Information Administration (EIA) reported that crude stocks climbed by 3.4 million barrels to 417.8 million barrels in the week ended November 13. This compared with expectations of a rise of just 58,000 barrels in a Reuters poll of analysts.
Meanwhile, the possibility of disruptions to oil supplies from the Middle East continues to remain a concern.
Iran's navy said three oil tankers travelling east of the Strait of Hormuz had been disabled by mines, Iranian media reported on Wednesday.
Investors are also looking towards a trilateral summit involving the leaders of the US, China and Russia for signals on the possibility of a negotiated end to the US-Iran war and Russia's invasion of Ukraine. Both conflicts have caused disruptions in global oil markets.
Separately, Ukrainian drone attacks have affected Russia's oil refining capacity. Reuters reported on Wednesday, citing industry sources, that the attacks have cut the combined crude processing volumes of Russian oil refineries by 45% since late October.

stories.headline: Three bank unions call for strike on December 3
stories.deck: Solidarity strike call given by AIBEA, AIBOA and BEFI is in support of IDBI Bank staff protesting government decision to sell stake to Fairfax
stories.bodyText:
Three prominent unions of bank employees and officers, AIBEA, AIBOA and BEFI, have jointly given a call for a solidarity strike on December 3 in support of IDBI Bank employees and officers opposing the government move to sell stake in the bank.
The United Forum of IDBI Officers and Employees have called for a strike on December 3, following a two-day strike earlier this month, with the government moving ahead with the stake sale to Fairfax Financial Holdings, leaders of the unions said in a statement on Thursday (November 19, 2026).
IDBI Bank is a profit-making bank and has total deposits of about ₹3.50 lakh crore and advances of ₹2.50 lakh crore, translating into a total business of ₹6 lakh crore. If it is sold to Fairfax, “this swadeshi bank will become a videshi bank. The decision to sell the bank to a foreign investor is totally unwarranted,” they said.
ALSO WATCH Watch: The ₹53,000 cr IDBI Bank deal: Did mega sell-off get valuation right? | Business Matters
AIBEA general secretary C.H. Venkatachalam, AIBOA general secretary Sanjay Khan and BEFI general secretary Debasish Basu Chaudhury said, “It is the experience in our country that public sector banks are the safety for the people’s savings. Many private banks have been closed down due to mismanagement, and people have lost their hard-earned savings. All these failed private banks were then taken over by public sector banks.”
The government, which with the Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC), holds 94% in IDBI Bank, is proposing to sell 60% to Fairfax.
“Banks represent the precious savings of the people, and privatisation and selling banks to private hands amounts to handing over the huge savings... Total deposits in the banks are more than ₹250 lakh crore, and this represents the savings of our people. This is the social capital with which we should ensure further economic development and progress of our nation,” the leaders of the All India Bank Employees’ Association, All India Bank Officers Association and Bank Employees Federation of India said

briefs.headline: Piramal Pharma to acquire remaining 26% stake in Yapan Bio
briefs.deck: With the acquisition, Piramal will fully embed Yapan’s advanced large molecule capabilities into its integrated service offering
briefs.bodyText:
Piramal Pharma will be increasing its stake in contract development and manufacturing organisation Yapan Bio from 74% to 100%.
Discussions with the shareholders of Yapan in this regard are under way. The final terms, including acquisition cost and the effective date, are yet to be finalised, Piramal Pharma said, announcing that the Administrative Committee of its Board has approved the exercise of the company’s call option to acquire the balance 26% equity stake. Upon completion of the transaction, Yapan will become a wholly owned subsidiary.
A CDMO based in Hyderabad’s Genome Valley, Yapan specialises in process development, characterisation and Phase I/II GMP manufacturing services for vaccines and biologics. Piramal Pharma initially in December 2021 acquired a 27.78% stake in Yapan Bio for more than ₹101 crore.
In August this year, Piramal said it has completed the acquisition of 1,46,400 equity shares from existing shareholders of Yapan for around ₹76 crore taking its shareholding, in the CDMO, from 33.33% to 74%.
With the acquisition, it will fully embed Yapan’s advanced large molecule capabilities into its integrated service offering, enabling the company to develop and scale complex biologic therapies with greater efficiency, Piramal had then said in a filing.
